sections.h2: Is Belton, TX a growing market for house sellers?
sections.html:
Belton is the seat of Bell County in Central Texas, and its population has climbed since 2010. The Census Bureau counted 18,216 residents in 2010 and 23,054 in 2020, then estimated 25,964 for July 1, 2025, a 12.7% rise over the 2020 estimates base.

Growth brings demand, yet a seller still has a tax bill, possibly tenants, and a deed to deal with. The sections below cover the Belton specifics first and the Texas rules after them.

sections.h2: How did Belton start out, and why does the creek matter to older lots?
sections.html:
A history the city publishes, written by a former librarian, says surveyors laid the town out in August 1850 as county seat of the newly organized Bell County. The first name was Nolandville; by 1851 it was Belton, and the town incorporated in 1852.

Nolan Creek ran near the courthouse square, and the first courthouse stood on blocks to ride out floods. A flood in 1913 is why one city park bears a family name. Anyone with an older, creek-side lot should ask about floodplain status. Limestone storefronts from the 1860s still stand downtown, which gives the older blocks their character.

  • Stagecoach and mail stop in the 1850s, Katy railroad depot by 1882
  • Baylor Female College, now the University of Mary Hardin-Baylor, was a new institution by the 1880s
  • Fort Hood and two large lakes brought a later surge of growth
  • Interstate 35 makes the city attractive to business and industry, per the city's history

sections.h2: What does Census data say about owning and renting in Belton?
sections.html:
The 2020-2024 midpoint for an owner-occupied Belton home is $258,700, and 56.0% of units are lived in by owners. Tenants pay a midpoint of $1,252 monthly, so rentals are a real part of the supply.

The city's land area is 20.23 square miles, up from 18.93 in 2010. Density rose from 962.3 residents per square mile in 2010 to 1,139.7 in 2020. The typical drive to work is 22.8 minutes, and 1,762 veterans live in the city. Fort Hood's arrival is part of Belton's growth story.

sections.h2: Who sends Belton property tax bills, and when do early-payment discounts apply?
sections.html:
Bell CAD appraises property and also takes tax payments. Its FAQ says statements go out every October covering the whole year, payment is due on receipt, and penalties begin on February 1 for anything left after January 31.

As the district describes it, paying in full earns a break for certain taxing entities: 3% off in October, 2% in November, 1% in December. January means the base tax with no discount and no penalty.

  • Pay online, by phone, or in person at any district office
  • After-hours drop box outside the Belton office
  • Deferral, quarterly installment and homestead delinquent installment agreements are explained on the district's site

sections.h2: How do you claim a homestead exemption in Bell County?
sections.html:
Apply from January 1 through April 30 of the tax year, at the district or online. Bell CAD says no yearly renewal is needed unless the chief appraiser requests one or you change homes, and it takes late applications for two years after the tax goes delinquent.

The home must have been yours and your residence on January 1, with no second homestead claimed. State law allows as many as 20 acres, though the district says an acre or less is typical. A mobile home owner who does not own the land can qualify with a title or a verified purchase contract.

Extra relief exists for older and disabled owners, and a surviving spouse aged 55 or more may keep the school tax ceiling. Disabled veterans need a VA letter showing a rating of at least 10%, and a 100% rating may support a full homestead exemption.

sections.h2: Does the 10% homestead cap change what a Belton buyer pays?
sections.html:
It limits assessed value only. Bell CAD explains that market value follows sales with no cap, while a homestead's assessed value can grow just 10% a year.

The limit starts after an owner has held the home through a full January 1. A buyer taking over a house that sold well above its old assessment could see the bill climb for several years until assessed value reaches market value.

sections.h2: What rules cover a short-term rental in Belton?
sections.html:
The city adopted its short-term rental ordinance on March 13, 2023, and each rental needs a city permit that lasts one year. The owner must file for renewal within 30 days of the expiration date.

No renewal happens until local hotel and motel occupancy tax has been paid. A rental that the owner does not occupy must stay at least 500 feet from another short-term rental. Each address needs its own application through the online portal, and income goes in there quarterly, entering zero for months without stays.

  • Apply and renew through the city's portal
  • One application per property address
  • The Planning Department answers questions on the process

sections.h2: What if a Belton landlord wants tenants gone before closing?
sections.html:
Texas calls for a written notice to vacate, giving at least three days unless the lease sets a different period. Delivery options include hand delivery, leaving it inside the unit, mail, or email when the lease allows.

A tenant who stays faces a justice court case, with a hearing 10 to 21 days after filing. Appeals to county court must come within five days of judgment. A writ of possession can issue after six days, with 24 hours of warning before removal. Build that schedule into the closing date, or negotiate a sale that leaves tenants in place.

sections.h2: How do foreclosure and tax liens reach a Belton house?
sections.html:
When a deed of trust grants power of sale, the lender can auction a Bell County house on a first Tuesday. The owner has 20 days after the default notice to reinstate, and the sale notice must go out 21 or more days beforehand.

Property tax sits under a separate lien that attaches each January 1 and follows the land through a sale. The person who owned the house on that date stays liable, so the title company should settle the year's bill at closing.

sections.h2: Where is a Belton deed filed?
sections.html:
The Bell County clerk records deeds for land in the county, and the deed needs a signature and an acknowledgment. Ask Bell CAD what it needs to update the owner name once the deed is filed.

The state clerk manual shows $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page, with other statutory charges beyond that. Ask the Bell County clerk for the full figure before you file.

faqs.q: When must a Belton homestead application be filed?
faqs.a: By April 30 for the tax year. Bell CAD still takes late applications for up to two years after the tax turns delinquent, and no yearly renewal is required.

faqs.q: Is there an early-pay discount on Belton property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, for certain entities. Bell CAD lists 3% in October, 2% in November and 1% in December, with the base amount due in January.

faqs.q: Can I rent a Belton house on a nightly basis?
faqs.a: Only with a city permit. Belton requires one for every short-term rental, renewed yearly, and a non-owner-occupied rental must sit 500 feet from any other.

faqs.q: If I sell a Belton house mid-year, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 carries the lien and the liability. Sellers and buyers usually divide the bill at closing through the title company.

faqs.q: Which office values my Belton house?
faqs.a: Bell CAD does, with offices in Belton, Killeen and Temple. The district says it normally reviews sales and properties every year.
